signal.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
signal.summary: On November 10, 2026, Google Cloud announced a U.S. preview of Gemini for healthcare, an enterprise system that combines specialized healthcare skills, clinical record connectors, controlled agents and audit trails. Read integrations for Epic and Oracle Health are listed among partner capabilities. The product is aimed at providers and payers, not at replacing clinical judgment or becoming a general consumer diagnosis service.

signal.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
signal.summary: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, powered by Gemini Decision 1, for probabilistic classification rather than general text generation. The announcement lists up to 1,000 questions per request, 256,000-token multimodal inputs and a $0.10 per million-input-token list price, with no output-token billing. SXF explains the difference between advertised model-compute speed and end-to-end latency and shows how to design human-review thresholds instead of treating a confidence score as proof.

signal.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
signal.summary: Google announced the global integration of Gemini 4 Hydrogen into Search on November 12, 2026, aiming to interpret complex, multi-part queries and present more visual, structured results with links to relevant sources. signal.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
signal.summary: The ggml-org team announced version 1.0.0 of the llama.cpp and ggml libraries on November 13, 2026, clarifying semantic-versioning contracts for public C interfaces. Future API or ABI-breaking changes trigger major-version increments, while compatible features and bug fixes use minor and patch increments. The milestone matters to application integrators and package maintainers; it is not a claim that all backends have identical behaviour or that throughput improved by a measured percentage.

signal.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
signal.summary: OpenAI announced on November 12, 2026 that it committed $2 million to a research network under the Coalition for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of AI after signing a charter at the Paris Peace Forum. The announced goal is shared scientific measurement of AI's risks and opportunities for children, with researcher control over findings and publication of inconclusive or negative results. SXF explains what the commitment actually funds in principle and which independent checks are still necessary before claiming improved child safety.
